title: Coherent comparison with a family of row colimits
statement: Use the fixed universes, small simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, transformations, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $I,J$ be small simplicial sets and $\mathcal E$ a quasicategory in a containing universe. Suppose given a coherent functor $L:\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal E$ and a coherent transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to\Delta_J L$ such that, for each $A:J\to\mathcal E$, the cocone $\eta_A:A\to\Delta_J L(A)$ is colimiting. Let $R:I\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)$ and $U:I\to\mathcal E$ be coherent diagrams and let $\alpha:R\to\Delta_J\circ U$ be a coherent transformation. Assume that for every vertex $i\in I$ the cocone $\alpha_i:R(i)\to\Delta_J U(i)$ is colimiting. Then there is a coherent equivalence $a:LR\to U$ and a homotopy, in the entire coherent transformation space, between $\alpha$ and $(\Delta_J a)\circ(\eta R)$. More precisely, the space of pairs consisting of $a$ and such a compatibility homotopy is contractible, and every comparison in this space is a coherent equivalence. No colimits other than the displayed $J$-colimits are assumed, and neither index is required to be sifted or weakly contractible.

source.place: Agent-formulated coherent row-colimit comparison extracted from the successive-colimit reconstruction of HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6 (printed p.507), referring to the absolute case of Lemma 5.5.2.3 (printed pp.463-464). The PDF was read online; this precise cylinder/mapping-space formulation is not quoted as a theorem of HTT. No Stacks tag states the quasicategorical result.

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)$ and $T=\Delta_J:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$. The functor-category clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $\mathcal D$ a quasicategory. Its dual cocone criterion, applied to the hypothesized $\eta_A$, says that for every $A\in\mathcal D$ and $x\in\mathcal E$ the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L(A),x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(A,T(x)),\qquad f\longmapsto T(f)\circ\eta_A,$$
is an equivalence. Thus the given coherent pair $(L,\eta)$ is universal-arrow data for the dual assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows], with full subcategory $\mathcal D_0=\mathcal D$. Enlarge the containing universe once so these functor categories and their diagram categories fit; $I,J$ remain small. No new colimit existence assumption is used.

source.place: Universal cocone criterion; verification of the dual universal-arrow hypothesis.

proof.text:
The dual coherent-diagram clause of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] therefore gives, for the given $R$ and $U$, the equivalence
$$\Phi:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)}(LR,U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal D)}(R,TU),\qquad a\longmapsto (Ta)\circ(\eta R).$$
Here the formula applies to the specified pair $(L,\eta)$, not merely to some new choice: the cited theorem's space of universal-arrow choices, including the functor and its universal transformation, is contractible. If its existence assertion first supplies $(L_0,\eta_0)$, connect that pair to $(L,\eta)$ in that space. The connection includes a coherent equivalence $e:L\simeq L_0$ and the compatibility $\eta_0\simeq(Te)\eta$. Precomposition with $eR$ identifies the two source mapping spaces, with inverse given by its coherent inverse; the compatibility identifies the two displayed composition maps. The formula for $(L_0,\eta_0)$ consequently implies the formula above. The cited evaluation compatibility makes evaluation of $\Phi$ at $i$ precisely $f\mapsto T(f)\eta_{R(i)}$.

source.place: Dual coherent-diagram mapping-space formula, including independence from universal-arrow choices.

proof.text: Both sides of $\Phi$ are Kan complexes by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Form its homotopy fiber $P_\alpha$ over the specified point $\alpha$. In the mapping-path model of [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion], a point of $P_\alpha$ is exactly a transformation $a:LR\to U$ and a path from $\Phi(a)$ to $\alpha$ in the entire target mapping space. Higher simplices retain both data and their compatibilities. Since $\Phi$ is an equivalence, that criterion makes $P_\alpha$ contractible. In particular it is nonempty: a weak equivalence to a point induces a bijection on components, whereas the empty space has no component. Choose one point for existence; the argument below applies to every point of this fiber. Reversing its Kan path gives the compatibility homotopy in either orientation.

source.place: Contractibility of the homotopy fiber of the full transformation-space equivalence.

proof.text:
Fix any $(a,h)\in P_\alpha$ and vertex $i\in I$. Write $A=R(i)$, $l=L(A)$, $u=U(i)$ and $a_i:l\to u$. Evaluation of $h$ gives $T(a_i)\eta_A\simeq\alpha_i$. By the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied now to the hypothesized colimiting $\alpha_i$ and test object $l$, there is $b_i:u\to l$ with $T(b_i)\alpha_i\simeq\eta_A$. Composition gives
$$T(b_i a_i)\eta_A\simeq\eta_A,\qquad T(a_i b_i)\alpha_i\simeq\alpha_i.$$
Apply the same criterion to $\eta_A$ with test object $l$, and to $\alpha_i$ with test object $u$. Each composition map is an equivalence of Kan mapping spaces, hence injective on components. The two displayed homotopies therefore imply $b_i a_i\simeq\mathrm{id}_l$ and $a_i b_i\simeq\mathrm{id}_u$. These are inverse-triangle witnesses, so $a_i$ is an equivalence. This is only a vertexwise argument; no coherent choice of the $b_i$ is required or asserted.

source.place: Comparison between the two initial cocones in each row; explicit two-sided inverse calculation.

proof.text: Every vertex component of $a$ is an equivalence by step 4. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] with shape $I$ and target $\mathcal E$ to conclude that $a:LR\to U$ is a coherent equivalence. This applies to every point of $P_\alpha$. Consequently requiring the comparison to be an equivalence removes no points or higher compatibility data from that fiber: the space of pairs asserted in the item is $P_\alpha$, already proved contractible in step 3. All tests used only the supplied $J$-colimits; the arguments impose no condition of siftedness or weak contractibility on either shape.

source.place: Pointwise detection of coherent equivalences; completion of the full comparison-space assertion.
